header: Date: 2026-10-20 | Time: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Evan Cole (Astra CTO), Maya Lin (Astra ML), Carlos Rivera (Astra Infra)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency/throughput) vs customer's baseline provider. Main takeaways: Redwood shows lower p95 tail on most configs, throughput comparable when using continuous batching; network variability noted on customer side; next steps include dedicated capacity test, quantized runs, and sharing raw logs and spreadsheet.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Mills: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check — can we do a quick roll call?
[00:07] Evan Cole: Yep Evan here, Maya and Carlos are on. Good morning.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Priya from Redwood, I'll walk through the numbers after Jordan sets context.
[00:19] Jordan Mills: Cool, so agenda — run through last week's benchmark, compare to your baseline provider, call out variance, then action items. If anything's off interrupt.
[00:31] Maya Lin: Sounds good, also we have network folks on standby if we need packet captures later.
[00:38] Priya Rao: Alright slide 1 — baseline runs. So we ran 3 configs: Hosted default, Hosted with batching tuned, and Quantized int8 on same GPU family. Baseline provider numbers we pulled from your perf logs — their p95 is around 420–480 ms on 256 tokens, p99 spikes to ~950 ms.
[01:01] Carlos Rivera: Those numbers align w/ what we saw last month, yes. Our concern is tail latency for user-facing chat.
[01:08] Priya Rao: Right, Redwood default hosted p95 is 290 ms, p99 610 ms in our runs, so roughly 30% better p95 and ~35-40% better p99 vs baseline for same token length. Throughput (tokens/sec) is similar when both sides use batching, but we see steadier throughput with continuous batching and KV cache.
[01:32] Evan Cole: How repeatable are those numbers? We saw variance before in your earlier run.
[01:35] Priya Rao: Good question — repeatability depends on network and cold-starts. We did 6 runs over 24 hours; median was consistent, variance came from a few outliers on the baseline provider that align with their idle scaling/GPUs warming. We can share full run logs.
[01:52] Jordan Mills: Note — some of the baseline spikes look like their autoscaler added capacity mid-run which caused serialization delays, not model computation time.
[02:00] Maya Lin: Interesting. Can you call out which kernel/runtime options you used? Our infra folks want to know specifics.
[02:06] Priya Rao: Yeah so we used our serving runtime with optimized attention kernels, continuous batching window 50 ms, max batch 64, KV cache enabled for repeated context, and mixed precision with selective int8 quantization for the quantized runs. I'll put exact run config in the spreadsheet.
[02:26] Carlos Rivera: When you say quantized, is that model conversion on your side or ours?
[02:30] Priya Rao: We did the quantize pipeline in our test cluster — it's the same binary we recommend for Dedicated. For private deployment we can walk through converting within your environment too.
[02:40] Evan Cole: Any observed accuracy regressions on int8?
[02:43] Priya Rao: Small delta on a few tokens in the eval set we used, mostly low-confidence paraphrases — we logged examples. Overall eval scores changed <1.5% on our prompt set.
[02:56] Maya Lin: Ok that's acceptable if the cost/latency gain is meaningful. What's the token/sec uplift on int8?
[03:02] Priya Rao: Int8 increased throughput by ~12-18% and reduced GPU memory footprint by ~20%, which helps packing more concurrent contexts per GPU.
[03:12] Jordan Mills: On cost basis that translated to about 15% lower per-token compute cost in our run, not counting network.
[03:20] Evan Cole: Network — we noticed your runs occasionally had longer tails when our region had higher egress jitter. How much of the tail is network vs compute?
[03:28] Priya Rao: From server-side logs, compute p95 remained steady; the long tails correlated with higher RTT on your side and occasional retries. We recommend a colocated VPC peering test or Dedicated in your preferred region to lower those bounds.
[03:45] Carlos Rivera: We can try a peering test; need to confirm our security team okays the routing.
[03:50] Jordan Mills: Totally — we can provide a minimal peering playbook. Also, Dedicated capacity with reserved GPUs removes autoscaling jitter and can improve p99 significantly.
[04:00] Maya Lin: If we do Dedicated, what's the onboarding time?
[04:03] Priya Rao: Typically 2–4 weeks for onboarding and network setup, less if we do managed private deployment.
[04:09] Evan Cole: Security — our auditors will need SOC2 docs, KMS details, and audit logs. Do you have those?
[04:14] Jordan Mills: Yes — we'll attach SOC2 report, architecture diagram for key management (KMS/HSM options), and sample audit logs. I'll send the security pack after the call.
[04:23] Maya Lin: Great. Back to benchmarks — can you run a 512-token context test? Our production uses longer contexts and we want to see scaling.
[04:30] Priya Rao: Yes, we scheduled a 512-token run as part of next week's dedicated test. We'll include p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and memory utilization.
[04:38] Carlos Rivera: Also can you include cold-start numbers? The baseline provider's cold starts are painful.
[04:42] Priya Rao: We'll include cold-start 95th as well. For cold-start we saw baseline provider hitting multi-second spikes; Redwood cold-starts are 700–1200 ms depending on context length.
[04:54] Jordan Mills: Quick note — cost modeling attached to spreadsheet shows Redwood unit cost parity or better vs baseline when using batching + quantization; raw per-token compute cost improves with Dedicated.
[05:05] Evan Cole: OK, one hesitation from procurement is vendor lock for Dedicated or Private. Can Redwood support exit data export and a portable runtime?
[05:13] Jordan Mills: Yes — we support model version pinning and can provide a private deployment bundle; we also publish runtime containers and conversion tools so you can run a compatible runtime in-house if needed.
[05:22] Maya Lin: Good to hear. Any competitors in the running? We are also testing Anthropic and an in-house system.
[05:28] Priya Rao: We tried Anthropic in the same test matrix — throughput comparable but p99s were higher in their managed offering for this workload; we'll include those columns in the sheet as well.
[05:38] Carlos Rivera: Are there any configuration knobs we should try on our side to reduce network tail?
[05:42] Priya Rao: Yes — persistent connections, keepalive tuning, client-side batching of small requests, and local NLBs to reduce RTT. We'll add a short checklist.
[05:52] Jordan Mills: Let's talk schedule — we propose a dedicated capacity run next Wed, quantized runs by Fri, and deliver the spreadsheet + raw logs tomorrow EOD. Does that work?
[06:01] Evan Cole: Next Wed is fine for the dedicated run — we need at least 48 hours notice for infra provisioning.
[06:07] Maya Lin: We'll aim to send the production token distribution by Tuesday.
[06:11] Carlos Rivera: And I'll coordinate with security on the peering approval.
[06:15] Priya Rao: Thanks — I'll follow up with the run configs and links.
[06:19] Jordan Mills: Anything else?
[06:21] Evan Cole: One small ask — can you show a cost scenario for 1M active users/day with 2 requests/user average? Just a back-of-envelope in the pricing doc.
[06:29] Jordan Mills: Yep I'll include a couple of scenarios (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
[06:34] Maya Lin: ok thanks everyone.
[06:36] Priya Rao: I'll send the sheet and logs after the call.
[06:40] Jordan Mills: Recap — Redwood to share spreadsheet + raw logs, SE to run int8 and 512 token runs, schedule Dedicated test next Wed, customer to provide traffic trace and approve peering. Action items in CRM. Thanks all.
[06:52] Evan Cole: Thanks, bye.
[06:54] End of recording
notes: Transcript contains some auto-transcription errors; product names sometimes transcribed loosely (e.g., KV cache -> K V cache). Links referenced during call: benchmark spreadsheet (link shared in chat), security pack (to be sent by Jordan).
